# example:weather-client

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

The Java client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request), generated by [Crucible](https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible) from the service's model.

## Install

```xml
<dependency><groupId>example</groupId><artifactId>weather-client</artifactId><version>0.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version></dependency>
```

The package is `example:weather-client`, version `0.0.0-SNAPSHOT`; code refers to it as `example.weather`.

## Create a client

```java
import example.weather.ClientConfig;
import example.weather.WeatherClient;

ClientConfig config = new ClientConfig();
config.token = () -> System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
WeatherClient client = new WeatherClient(config);
```

`ClientConfig.token` is a `Supplier<String>` of the bearer token, called for every attempt, so a refreshed token is used. The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request.

## Call an operation

`getCity` calls `GetCity`. Every operation has a method like it.

```java
import example.weather.ClientConfig;
import example.weather.WeatherClient;
import example.weather.model.GetCityInput;
import example.weather.model.GetCityOutput;
import example.weather.model.NotFoundError;
import java.time.Instant;

public class GetCityExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
        ClientConfig config = new ClientConfig();
        config.token = () -> System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
        WeatherClient client = new WeatherClient(config);

        // Values from the model's example "Read a city".
        GetCityInput input = GetCityInput.builder()
            .cityId("c-0a1b2c3d")
            .at(Instant.parse("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z"))
            .build();

        try {
            GetCityOutput output = client.getCity(input);
            System.out.println(output.city());
            System.out.println(output.forecast());
            System.out.println(output.requestId());
        } catch (NotFoundError error) {
            System.err.println("NotFoundError (HTTP " + error.status() + "): " + error.message());
        }
    }
}
```

## Pagination

A paginated operation also has a `<operation>Pages` method returning a lazy `java.util.Iterator` of pages (`client.listCitiesPages(input)`), and `<operation>PagesAsync` returning a `Flow.Publisher`: each page is one response, and it stops when the response carries no next token. Each operation also has an `<operation>Async` method returning a `CompletableFuture`, and an overload taking a `Consumer` of the input's builder.

```java
import example.weather.ClientConfig;
import example.weather.WeatherClient;
import example.weather.model.ListCitiesInput;
import example.weather.model.ListCitiesOutput;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.List;

public class ListCitiesPagesExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
        ClientConfig config = new ClientConfig();
        config.token = () -> System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
        WeatherClient client = new WeatherClient(config);

        // Values from the model's example "List the first page".
        ListCitiesInput input = ListCitiesInput.builder()
            .maxResults(2)
            .tags(List.of("coastal", "capital"))
            .build();

        // Each page is one response; the iterator sends `nextToken` for the next.
        Iterator<ListCitiesOutput> pages = client.listCitiesPages(input);
        while (pages.hasNext()) {
            ListCitiesOutput page = pages.next();
            System.out.println(page.cities());
        }
    }
}
```

## Errors

Each modelled error is an unchecked exception class in `example.weather.model`, extending `example.weather.WeatherException` and `ServiceError`: catch it and read its accessors, and `status()`, `requestId()` and `headers()`. Transport failures throw `NetworkError`.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. An idempotency token the caller leaves unset is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: `createCity` (`clientToken`). Set `ClientConfig.maxAttempts` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), and `timeout`, `baseDelay` and `maxDelay` for the call budget and backoff.
